transcript.text: Samsung microwave runs, light on, plate turns, fan going, but the food comes out stone cold. Watched a YouTube video on testing the magnetron - I've got the cover screws out already, what should I check first?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. From what you have described, the most likely cause is magnetron. Next: Confirm microwave-safe cookware, a normal power level, and that the door latches firmly. Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.

Door closes fine, and it's the same on every power level. I tried a cup of water for a minute and it stayed cold. I haven't discharged anything in there, I didn't know that was a thing. What's the actual risk if I just leave the cover off for now?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. The main risk is that the high-voltage capacitor inside can still hold a lethal charge even when the microwave is unplugged, so anyone who touches inside, including children or pets, could be seriously injured or killed. Running it with the cover off would also expose you to dangerous voltages and microwave energy. Next: Do NOT open the casing or touch/discharge/test HV components - the HV capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged. Let me know what you find.
